harness.system_prompt:
You are helm, an agent at the conn of the JobyCorp fleet. Be direct and concise.

Working method: survey before you read. `tree` shows where the mass is, `outline` gives a file's skeleton, `grep` with `context` replaces a read after every hit, `sgrep` answers structural questions (call sites, shapes), and `read` windows are for judgment, not indexing. Files go through the file tools: `read` not cat/sed, `grep` not grep/rg, `glob` not find, `edit`/`write` not sed or heredocs. Bash runs things: builds, tests, mix tasks. A dev server is a server job — `bash(background: true, server: true, port:)`: no deadline, a note when its port answers, `job(action: "wait")` waits, `job(action: "kill")` stops it; other long commands run with `bash(background: true)`. Never detach a process yourself, and never signal one you did not start. Several tool calls in one round are welcome when they are independent. Commands must not wait on stdin: pass scripts with `-e` or a file, never an interactive `iex`. Read enough to act, act, verify, and stop.
harness.nudge: Continue until every requirement in the task is done, then reply with the one-line summary.
harness.last_call: Round cap reached — this is the last call. Stop anything you started (background jobs, servers), then reply with the one-line summary: what is done and what is not. No further work.
harness.nudge_policy: once, only after a narrated or blank ending; otherwise abandoned
harness.brief:
# JobyCorp website — design brief

JobyKit is already installed and `benchapp` is a generated JobyKit app that
compiles, boots, and passes its tests. Work inside `benchapp`. Follow the
guidelines in `benchapp/AGENTS.md` and the design direction in
`benchapp/DESIGN.md`; where `DESIGN.md` and this brief differ, this brief
wins.

## The client

JobyCorp is a local AI research company. It runs analysis and benchmarks of
local LLMs on its own hardware and shares the research openly with the
community. The site is JobyCorp's public home: it should tell a visitor
what JobyCorp does, show that the work is real and rigorous, and invite
them to read and follow it.

Use only the facts above. Do not invent statistics, customer names, team
members, awards, dates, or product names. Where a section wants a number
or a name you have not been given, write copy that does not need one.

## Scope

This is a design task. Build the visual identity, the layout, the copy, and
the components. Do not add application features: no forms that submit, no
live data, no countdowns. Static content and navigation only. The app's
databases already exist so the dev server boots; do not add tables,
migrations, schemas, or any use of the Repo — the site has no data.

1. Remove every trace of the generator's demo: the stock `simple_nav`
   header, the "built with" footer, the welcome content of HomeLive, and
   every link to `/design`, `/custom-designs`, and `/design.json`. Those
   pages exist for inspecting the kit and are not part of the product;
   leave their routes in place but nothing on the site may link to or
   mention them.
2. Three pages, all on the same layout: `/` (the landing page),
   `/research` (what JobyCorp publishes and how it tests), and `/about`
   (who JobyCorp is and why the work is shared).
3. A top navigation bar in `Layouts.app` with id `main-nav` that marks the
   current page's link with `aria-current="page"`, collapses behind a
   toggle button with id `nav-toggle` at phone widths, and carries the
   kit's theme toggle with id `theme-toggle`, usable at both widths.
4. A footer that belongs to JobyCorp.
5. The landing page: a hero that says what JobyCorp does in one sentence, a
   section on the research (what is measured and how), a section on the
   hardware and method (local models, local hardware, results published in
   full), and a closing call to action to read the research. Sections are
   yours to add or merge; every section must earn its place.
6. At least one composite component of your own, registered in the
   DesignManifest with a preview (host composites show on
   `/custom-designs`), used on more than one page.

## Design requirements

- Light and dark themes, both finished, with the palette `DESIGN.md`
  defines applied to the `light` and `dark` themes in `app.css` (keep
  those two names; the theme toggle switches by them). Phone and desktop,
  both finished. No horizontal overflow at 390 px. Body text contrast at
  least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1 in both themes.
- The installed heroicon set is `deps/heroicons/optimized/24/outline`
  (and `solid`); the name is `hero-` plus the file name without `.svg`.
- `Layouts.app` and a LiveView's `render/1` are exempt from the lint's
  unmarked-component rule. `mix format` (part of precommit) re-indents
  HEEx — re-read a block before editing it after a format.
- Every icon name you use must exist in the installed heroicon set; check
  before you use it. A blank icon is a defect.
- Copy is concise: headings of a few words, sentences a visitor can read
  at a glance. Copy is about JobyCorp and its research, never about the
  component kit, the framework, or this task.
- Compose the kit's registered wrappers; raw HTML primitives are a lint
  failure. Lint must be clean.

## Tests

7. Existing tests must pass; update any test that referred to removed
   demo content. No new features. Add a render test for each new page.

## Constraints

- The dev server must run on port 4099; `PORT` is already set. Do not use
  any other port. Do not stop or kill processes you did not start.
- Look at every page at 1440 and 390, in both themes, as you build —
  the preview tool has viewport, scheme, click, wait_for and evaluate.
  A scratch directory for probes, notes and screenshots is `../scratch`
  (outside `benchapp`); nothing there is graded.
- When `mix precommit` and `mix joby_kit.lint` both pass, reply with a
  one-line summary. Green is the end: do not re-verify, do not take
  more screenshots.

desktop.text:
JobyCorp
Home
Research
About
How a run is measured

JobyCorp publishes analysis and benchmarks of local LLMs. Each result is a run record — the configuration, the method, and the measured quantities — published in full rather than as a summary.

method

The test, in order

The method is a sequence, run the same way every time, so a result means the same thing wherever it appears.

1
Name the model and the exact build that runs.
2
Record the hardware, the software, and every setting before a run.
3
Answer a fixed prompt set on the local machine.
4
Capture the quantities above into one run record.
5
Publish the record, the method, and the configuration in full.

run record

model
identifier
hardware
identifier
context length
tokens
throughput
tokens / s
latency
ms / token
quality
score
The record a run produces — field and unit, no invented values.

publication

Every result, published in full

A result is worth little if the reader cannot check it. Each published run carries the configuration, the method, and the run record, so anyone can reproduce the measurement instead of taking it on faith.
